Ashes in the Wind: Volcanoes, End Times, and the Fiery Prelude to Tribulation

Introduction: When the Earth Speaks, Listen

Throughout history, volcanoes have stood as awe-inspiring monuments of Earth’s raw power—towering mountains that breathe fire and smoke, reshaping landscapes in minutes and reminding mankind of how small it truly is. In recent years, however, the frequency and intensity of volcanic activity have escalated in ways that even seasoned geologists find alarming. What’s more, many believers in the Word of God are beginning to see these fiery eruptions as more than just geological phenomena—they see them as apocalyptic warnings etched in magma and ash.

Could it be that the earth is not just cracking—but groaning? Is the increase in global volcanic eruptions a geological fluke, or is it the fulfillment of prophetic warnings Jesus gave nearly 2,000 years ago?

This essay will examine the current condition of the world’s volcanoes, compare those conditions to biblical prophecy, and explore how such natural upheavals may foreshadow or play an active role in the oncoming Tribulation.

Part 1: A World on Fire — The Current Condition of Global Volcanoes

As of mid-2025, we are witnessing a near-simultaneous flare-up of volcanic activity across multiple continents and oceans. Here is a brief overview of some of the most significant volcanoes currently erupting or threatening to do so:

1.1 Mount Etna (Italy)

On June 2, 2025, Mount Etna, one of the most active volcanoes in the world, had its largest eruption in over a decade. Spectacular lava fountains, pyroclastic flows, and choking clouds of ash rose into the atmosphere. Tourists fled down blackened slopes as the mountain roared to life.

1.2 Kīlauea (Hawai‘i, USA)

This iconic volcano resumed its activity in December 2024, with a series of vigorous lava fountains and summit collapses. Episode 23 in May 2025 included fountains reaching over 1,000 feet high. The USGS warns Episode 24 may begin soon.

1.3 Kanlaon (Philippines)

Mount Kanlaon exploded in May 2025, sending ash 4,500 meters into the air and triggering destructive pyroclastic flows. Crops were destroyed, flights canceled, and mass evacuations carried out.

1.4 Axial Seamount (Pacific Ocean)

This underwater volcano lies a mile beneath the Pacific Ocean and is expected to erupt again in 2025. Over 1,000 small earthquakes a day have been recorded, and the seafloor is bulging—a clear sign of magma buildup.

1.5 Sakurajima (Japan), Popocatépetl (Mexico), and Icelandic Volcanoes

Other highly active volcanic systems are also showing signs of escalation. From Japan to Iceland to the Andes, the earth seems to be hissing, boiling, and preparing to vent with global consequences.

This isn’t normal background noise. It’s a planetary crescendo.

Part 2: The Bible and the Language of Fire

The Bible repeatedly portrays volcanic-like activity when describing God’s wrath and the end of days.

2.1 The Earth Will Burn: Prophecies of Judgment

“The earth is utterly broken down, the earth is clean dissolved, the earth is moved exceedingly.”
– Isaiah 24:19

“For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury…”
– Isaiah 66:15

When God pours out judgment, fire often accompanies it—whether it be Sodom and Gomorrah, the plagues of Egypt, or the judgments in Revelation. The earth is not immune from divine anger; it is the canvas upon which God often paints His justice.

2.2 Literal Fire in the Book of Revelation

The opening of the seventh seal unleashes trumpet judgments upon the earth in Revelation 8. The first few trumpets look suspiciously like natural disasters intensified to a supernatural scale:
•“And the first angel sounded, and there followed hail and fire mingled with blood, and they were cast upon the earth…” (Revelation 8:7)
•“And the second angel sounded, and as it were a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea…” (Revelation 8:8)
